subject: BlueOak - request for deletion evidence and certification of ephemeral debug logs
messages:
From: Anita Patel <anita.patel@blueoakpharma.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueOak Pharma Compliance <compliance@blueoakpharma.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: proof of deletion for ephemeral debug/session logs (SOC 2 audit)

Hi Sofia,

We are preparing evidence for our upcoming SOC 2 Type II review and need confirmation on Redwood's handling of ephemeral debug/session logs generated by our tenant during ingestion and processing. Specifically:  

- Can you provide a manifest or technical artifact showing that debug/session logs associated with tenant ID BO-8921 were purged on 2026-11-26 per our agreed 30-day ephemeral retention?
- If full manifests are not shareable, would a signed attestation plus a generated manifest (filenames + SHA256) suffice for the auditor?
- Please confirm whether any backup or archival path retains those logs beyond the ephemeral window, and if so what process is used to remove them.

We need this by COB Nov 27 to include in the audit binder. Let me know if you need a POA or an NDA amendment.

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Patel
Head of Compliance
BlueOak Pharma
[attachment: requested_log_scope.xlsx]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Anita Patel <anita.patel@blueoakpharma.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: proof of deletion for ephemeral debug/session logs (SOC 2 audit)

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide a signed attestation and a generated manifest (filename + SHA256 + deletion timestamp) that auditors typically accept. A couple of clarifying questions before I loop in infra:  

1) Which BlueOak tenant timestamps should we scope to? (you mentioned BO-8921; confirm whether to include the week of 2026-10-27 through 2026-11-26)
2) Do you need evidence that recovery snapshots/backups were also scanned/cleared, or only production debug/session streams?

I'll bring Ben in on the retention/backups detail and Marissa on the formal attestation. We aim to hit your COB 11/27 timeline.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Trust Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: proof of deletion for ephemeral debug/session logs (SOC 2 audit)

Sofia / Marissa — infra update for BlueOak request:  

- Scope confirmed: tenant BO-8921, window 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-26.
- Debug/session logs are written to transient S3 buckets with lifecycle rules (non-versioned). We run a nightly rotation job that compacts and deletes entries older than 30 days; for the BO-8921 window the purge job ran 2026-11-26T02:15:12Z.
- No snapshot replication is configured for those transient buckets. Long-term backups (RDS snapshots) do not contain raw debug/session payloads — we persist aggregated telemetry only.

I exported a manifest of deleted object keys and computed SHA256 hashes; sample lines are attached. We redacted PII and internal tokens from the filenames in the manifest per our disclosure policy. Full manifest (sanitized) attached: blueoak_deletion_manifest_20261126.csv. Also attached our log rotation policy doc for auditor context: redwood-log-rotation-policy-2026.pdf.

Notes: if the auditor needs S3 lifecycle job run logs, we can provide a time-series extract but will need to scrub system usernames.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Infrastructure Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: blueoak_deletion_manifest_20261126.csv]
[attachment: redwood-log-rotation-policy-2026.pdf]

From: Anita Patel <anita.patel@blueoakpharma.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: proof of deletion for ephemeral debug/session logs (SOC 2 audit)

Thanks Ben and Sofia — that helps. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- The sanitized manifest looks good for the auditor. They prefer the SHA256 column to validate deletion events — can you confirm the hash algorithm used and that it was calculated prior to deletion?
- We will accept a signed attestation PDF on Redwood letterhead referencing the manifest and the purge timestamp. Please include a named Redwood contact (security or SRE) who can answer follow-up technical questions during the audit window (Dec 6–10).

If you can get the attestation by 11/27 and the manifest checksum confirmation, we can slot this into our binder.

Regards,
Anita
[--- quoted below ---]

Subject: BlueOak - deletion attestation and checksum confirmation

Hi Anita — attaching the signed attestation and confirming the checksum details you requested. Summary: 

- Hash algorithm: SHA-256. Hashes were computed as part of the manifest generation step immediately prior to the purge job (timestamp 2026-11-26T02:12:58Z in our run log).
- Attached artifacts: blueoak_deletion_manifest_20261126.csv (sanitized manifest, includes object key, SHA256, deletion_timestamp), and attestation_signed_blueoak_20261127.pdf (signed by Marissa Cole, Head of Trust Operations).
- Backup confirmation: there are no backup or archival pathways that store raw debug/session payloads for BO-8921. Aggregated telemetry is retained in analytics stores per the retention schedule documented in redwood-log-rotation-policy-2026.pdf.
- Audit contact: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com) will be available for technical questions during Dec 6–10.

Links: I uploaded the artifacts to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cEXAMPLE (read-only). HubSpot record for this request: HS-452117.

Please reply if the auditor needs any additional material; otherwise we'll consider this request closed after you acknowledge receipt.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Trust Manager
Redwood Inference
